Old French ( franceis , françois , romanz ; French : ancien français [ɑ̃sjɛ̃ fʁɑ̃sɛ] ) was the language spoken in most of the northern half of France approximately between the late 8th [ 2 ] and mid-14th centuries. Rather than a unified language , Old French was a group of Romance dialects , mutually intelligible yet diverse . These dialects came to be collectively known as the langues d'oïl , contrasting with the langues d'oc , the emerging Occitano-Romance languages of Occitania , now Southern France .
